FROM CONSTELLATIONS TO COMPUTE CELLS

Space computing is
a system-level question.

Faster accelerators are only part of the answer. Satellites move, models span devices, and requests share network resources.

A moving network

Distance, visibility, and link availability evolve with orbital geometry. The physical scene defines the resources that execution can use.

A distributed model

Model ranks span accelerators and satellites. Kernel dependencies, parallel deployment, and collective communication shape progress.

A shared system

Input delivery, KV readiness, batch scheduling, and network contention all contribute to the time a request takes to complete.

Evaluate a specified system design—from physical configuration to end-to-end serving behavior.

OBSERVE

FOLLOW A REQUEST

From arrival to the next token.

Follow a request from ground delivery through Compute Cell execution to token return.

→→→

REQUEST READINESS

A request enters only when it is ready.

Input delivery, predecessor completion, and KV readiness gate admission to the target Cell. A migration must also satisfy model, KV format, and parallel-layout compatibility.

INTERPRETABLE PERFORMANCE MODELING

Compute and communication.
Connected by dependencies.

Model execution time and data movement together to explain where the system spends time.

COMPUTE

From a batch to kernel time.

Midlayer or Roofline is selected as the global compute mode. Model configuration, hardware profiles, and supported parallel deployments determine the execution path.

COMMUNICATION

Protocol-aware latency.
Resource-aware progress.

Communication combines protocol-aware estimates with flow-level resource sharing where applicable. Cross-satellite transfers consume the capacity of their paths and shared resources.

TTFT

Time to first token

Trace the path from request arrival to the first returned output token.

TOKEN TIMING

Decode progress

Inspect output-token timing alongside scheduling, computation, and communication events.

THROUGHPUT

System-level output

Interpret serving throughput together with request completion and execution traces.

CASE STUDIES

Three scenarios for
inference in orbit.

Compare satellite links, task assignment and request scheduling.

Ring→Full mesh

CASE STUDY I · COMPUTE FORMATION

How should satellites in a formation connect?

With the same total bandwidth, direct links between satellites that often exchange data can shorten inference latency.

Relay→Cell

CASE STUDY II · CONSTELLATION ACCESS AND LOAD DISTRIBUTION

When ground sites send requests at once, how can the constellation serve more of them?

Relays can ease local congestion by sending tasks to cells with spare capacity.

Ground⇄Cell

CASE STUDY III · MULTI-TURN INFERENCE SCHEDULING

How can users get a faster response to a follow-up?

Keeping follow-ups on the same cell lets it reuse cached context and return the first token sooner in long conversations.

Install from source

Clone, build and run

cd AsterMind

bash scripts/install-ubuntu-deps.sh
python3.12 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
bash scripts/build.sh
bash scripts/run.sh
